body: Destiny of an Emperor is Capcom's NES role-playing adaptation of Hiroshi Motomiya's Tenchi wo Kurau manga. Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei begin by opposing the Yellow Turban rebels, then become involved in a campaign across a divided China. Towns, travel and battles provide the structure of a console role-playing adventure, while generals take the place of a conventional small heroic party. The story draws on the Three Kingdoms tradition, giving familiar historical and literary figures new roles within a journey shaped around Liu Bei's victories.

Many encounters include named generals who can later be recruited. After a defeat, an opponent may offer to join in exchange for money or horses, turning an enemy into another possible member of the army. The active group has room for fighters, reserves and a tactician whose abilities can be used during battle. Choosing the next recruit therefore involves more than collecting names. The force needs people suited to its current opposition, and some generals remain useful longer than others as the campaign develops.

Battles offer attacks and tactics, with an All-Out option that resolves easier encounters rapidly under computer control. It sacrifices the player's detailed decisions in exchange for speed, making it useful when the outcome already looks secure. Visiting settlements and recruiting further officers then returns attention to the wider campaign. Released in Japan in 1989 and North America in 1990, Destiny of an Emperor gives the army an unusually personal character: the commander faced on one road may be fighting beside the player on the next.
